The trip, top to bottom

One sentence per event, no fluff. 15 days, Sat Apr 17 – Sat May 1, 2027, for Kevin, Arwen, and Evan.

Group: 3 travelers Days: 15 total Hanoi: 2 nights Ha Giang Loop: 3 days · 2 nights Ninh Binh: 2 nights Sleeper train: 1 night Hoi An: 6 nights (Apr 25–30) Flights: Booked (Kevin & Arwen)
Day 1 · Sat Apr 17

Kevin & Arwen fly out of Tampa at 10:20 AM — KE7122 / KE036 / KE447 via Atlanta and Seoul, 24h 15m, 2 stops — night on the plane, arriving Hanoi 9:35 PM on Sun Apr 18. Evan is not on this booking.

Day 2 · Sun Apr 18

Land at Hanoi (HAN) at 9:35 PM, Grab to the Old Quarter, check in, and keep it light — night 1 in Hanoi.

Day 3 · Mon Apr 19

Full buffer day in Hanoi for jet lag — eat, wander, early night — night 2 in Hanoi.

Day 4 · Tue Apr 20

Early transfer Hanoi → Ha Giang City, meet your three Easy Rider drivers, and ride Loop day 1 — night 1 on the Loop.

Day 5 · Wed Apr 21

Loop day 2 — the Ma Pi Leng pass and the boat on the Nho Que River — night 2 on the Loop.

Day 6 · Thu Apr 22

Loop day 3 back to Ha Giang City, then the long evening journey south to Ninh Binh — night 1 in Ninh Binh.

Day 7 · Fri Apr 23

Ninh Binh day — early Trang An boat ride and Hang Mua late in the day — night 2 in Ninh Binh.

Day 8 · Sat Apr 24

Ninh Binh in the day, then board the overnight sleeper train in the evening — one whole 4-berth cabin for the 3 of you, night on the train.

Day 9 · Sun Apr 25

Arrive Da Nang in the morning, Grab to Hoi An, check in, Old Town and the cooking class — night 1 in Hoi An.

Day 10 · Mon Apr 26

Ba Na Hills day trip from Hoi An — walk the Golden Bridge (the Golden Hands) before the crowds — night 2 in Hoi An.

Day 11 · Tue Apr 27

Light morning in Hoi An — coffee and a last slow Old Town walk in the core plan. No flight today; the flight home moved to Day 15 — night 3 in Hoi An.

The itinerary — day by day, for 3

Fifteen days, Sat Apr 17 – Sat May 1, 2027. The adventure is front-loaded while energy is highest — Hanoi buffer first, then the Loop — and the trip lands softly: one slow Ninh Binh stop, the sleeper train south, and Hoi An to finish. Every move has a route block; return legs get their own. If an embedded map ever looks blank in a preview, use the Open in Google Maps and directions links in each route block — those always work.

The north first: Hanoi → Ha Giang → Ninh Binh

Everything before the train is the adventure half. Everything after it is the exhale.

Day 1 · Sat Apr 17

Fly out — Tampa → Hanoi

Travel day. Night on the plane. Nothing else is planned today, on purpose.

The daily rule: check the airline app for Kevin & Arwen's seats together (22D/22E, then 42H/42G, then 34H/34G), passport names matching exactly, and bags checked through to HAN before you leave the check-in desk.
10:20 AMDepart Tampa (TPA) at 10:20 AM — KE7122 (op. Delta) TPA → ATL 10:20–11:56, KE036 ATL → ICN 1:25 PM–5:50 PM Sun Apr 18, KE447 ICN → HAN 6:55–9:35 PM — 24h 15m, 2 stops — arriving Hanoi (HAN) at 9:35 PM on Sun Apr 18. Booked for Kevin & Arwen (Flights tab).
In the airSleep on Vietnam time as early as you can. Westbound via Asia is the gentler direction — you land in the evening on Apr 18 and go straight into a normal Hanoi bedtime.
LayoverConfirm at check-in that bags are tagged through to HAN and all boarding passes for KE7122 / KE036 / KE447 are in hand before the first flight boards.

Day 2 · Sun Apr 18

Arrive Hanoi — buffer day, kept light on purpose

Night 1 of 2 in Hanoi. The first 1–3 days in Hanoi are the hard adjustment — traffic, noise, culture shock — so today is deliberately almost empty.

The daily rule: no plans that can be missed. Stay awake until a normal local bedtime, eat something real, and let the city come to you.
21:35Land at Noi Bai (HAN) at 9:35 PM. Clear arrivals, collect bags, and get on Hanoi time.
+1 hourGrab to the Old Quarter hotel. Vietnam has no Uber — Grab is the app. Order the larger 6/7-seat car for 3 people plus luggage; the price is fixed in the app before you ride.
AfternoonCheck in (2 rooms or one triple / family room), shower, short nap if you must — then get outside and walk the block so you sleep tonight.
EveningWander the Old Quarter near the hotel, first street food, early night. One traveler in the research wrote that Hanoi "almost swallowed me whole on Day 3" — by day three she was weaving through traffic like a local. Give it those days.

27–30 km · 35–60 min (75–90 at rush hour) · Larger Grab car for 3 + luggage

Day 3 · Mon Apr 19

Hanoi — the full buffer day

Night 2 of 2 in Hanoi. Jet lag fades today; tomorrow the Loop starts, so tonight ends early.

The daily rule: pack the Loop daypacks tonight — what each of you carries on the bikes for 3 days is listed in Logistics. Big bags stay behind in storage.
MorningSlow start, big breakfast, coffee. Walk Hoan Kiem Lake while it's still cool.
MiddayOld Quarter at your own pace — street food, the lanes around Hang Ma, no timed tickets, nothing that punishes a tired group.
AfternoonConfirm tomorrow with the Loop operator in writing: pickup time and place, 3 riders with 3 drivers, private-room homestay upgrade, and where the big bags are stored (Hanoi hotel or operator storage — see Logistics).
EveningEarly dinner, daypacks packed, alarms set. Tomorrow is an early start.
Getting aroundOn foot in the Old Quarter; Grab (no Uber in Vietnam) for anything farther.
Food pickBún chả for lunch — the Hanoi classic — and egg coffee after.
To bookHa Giang Loop — Not booked. Licensed operator only, 3-day Easy Rider, 3 riders + 3 drivers, private rooms.
Sleep tonightHanoi — Old Quarter hotel, night 2 of 2.
Transport and logisticsBig luggage goes into storage tomorrow morning (hotel or operator — Logistics). On the bikes: one small daypack each.
Maps — Day 3Hoan Kiem Lake → · Hang Ma Street →
Day 4 · Tue Apr 20

Hanoi → Ha Giang — Loop day 1

Night 1 of 2 on the Loop. Three riders, three drivers, daypacks only.

The daily rule: passengers only — do not self-drive this road as beginners. Licensed operator, written contract, helmets on. Speak up if a driver speeds.
EarlyTransfer Hanoi → Ha Giang City (~300 km, 6–8h by sleeper bus or limousine van — usually booked by your Loop operator; confirm the exact pickup when you book). Arrive, breakfast, and hand the big bags to storage.
MiddayMeet your three Easy Riders — one licensed local driver per traveler — and ride out toward Yen Minh and the Dong Van side of the loop. Riding days run roughly 8am–5pm with stops once you're on the loop proper.
EveningHomestay dinner. Book the private-room upgrade for the group — a double plus a single/twin, or a family room — not dorm beds.

Day 5 · Wed Apr 21

Ha Giang Loop day 2 — Ma Pi Leng & the Nho Que River

Night 2 of 2 on the Loop. The big scenery day — and the one every passenger account calls the highlight of the whole trip.

The daily rule: check the mountain weather with your drivers at breakfast — fog and rain change the pass timing, and the operator reroutes if they say so.
MorningRide the Ma Pi Leng pass — the cliff road above the Nho Que gorge, the signature stretch of the loop.
MiddayBoat on the Nho Que River (included in typical packages) — the gorge from water level after seeing it from the top.
AfternoonRide on toward the Meo Vac side. Expect stiff knees and a sore seat by now — every passenger account mentions it; the small seat cushion each of you packed earns its place today.
EveningSecond homestay night. Early bed — tomorrow is the longest day of the trip.
Getting aroundEasy Rider bikes all day, drivers' call on stops and weather.
Food pickHomestay dinner night two — plus whatever the roadside stop your drivers pick at lunch; trust them.
To bookNothing new today — the Loop package covers it. Tips for drivers are not included — bring cash dong for them.
Sleep tonightLoop homestay, private rooms for the group, night 2 of 2.
Transport and logisticsStill daypacks only. Cash matters up here — cards are not the Loop's payment method.
Maps — Day 5Ma Pi Leng Pass → · Nho Que River →
Day 6 · Thu Apr 22

Loop day 3, then the long run south to Ninh Binh

Night 1 of 2 in Ninh Binh. This is the longest travel day of the trip — say it plainly: Loop finish plus roughly 9–11 hours of road south, arriving late. Nothing is planned at the far end except a bed.

The daily rule: confirm tonight's onward transport with the operator before the last Loop leg starts — bus times, the Hanoi change, and who is holding your bags at each end.
DaytimeFinal Loop leg back to Ha Giang City — the longest ride of the three days (~140 km in one account). Collect stored bags, shower at the hostel (operators typically include the stop).
EveningHa Giang → Hanoi by sleeper bus (7–8h), then Hanoi → Tam Coc, Ninh Binh by limousine van (2–2.5h) — or the operator's through-arrangement if your package strings it together. If your big bags were stored in Hanoi, this is where you collect them on the way through.
LateArrive Tam Coc late, check in, sleep. Trang An waits until Day 7 — do not try to do anything tonight.

Day 7 · Fri Apr 23

Ninh Binh — Trang An boats & Hang Mua

Night 2 of 2 in Ninh Binh. The slow day the Loop earns you.

The daily rule: boats first, steps later — Trang An early beats the heat and the day-trip buses from Hanoi; Hang Mua is a late-day view.
07:00Trang An boat ride — 2.5–3 hours through caves and temples, the consensus top pick over Tam Coc's own boat. Pick one boat ride, not both.
MiddayBack to Tam Coc for lunch and a genuinely lazy afternoon — pool, nap, laundry. You are one long day out from the Loop and one long night out from the train.
Late dayHang Mua — climb the ~500 steps for the river-and-karst panorama in the best light of the day.

Day 8 · Sat Apr 24

Ninh Binh by day, sleeper train by night

Night on the train — one whole 4-berth cabin, just for the 3 of you.

The daily rule: be at Ninh Binh station early with all 3 passports — sleeper tickets are name-checked, and names must match passports exactly.
DaytimeUnhurried Ninh Binh: Tam Coc's own boat or the village by bike if yesterday left energy, a long lunch, bags repacked. Keep the afternoon loose — tonight is a travel night.
Early eveEarly dinner in Tam Coc, then Grab to Ninh Binh station (~7–10 km). Larger car for 3 + bags — no Uber in Vietnam, Grab is the app.
21:57Board SE19, the soft-sleeper overnight train south (SE3 at 21:36 is the fallback). Your cabin: a lockable, air-conditioned 4-berth — you fill 3 berths and book all 4 so no stranger takes the fourth. Times wobble by minutes between sources; recheck on dsvn.vn at booking.

Day 9 · Sun Apr 25

Arrive Da Nang → Hoi An — Old Town & cooking class

Night 1 of 6 in Hoi An, the final destination. Da Nang itself gets no night — you pass through it this morning and day-trip back out tomorrow.

The daily rule: train mornings run late and tired — check in and nap first, sights second. The Old Town is best at dusk anyway.
11:35Arrive Da Nang station. Larger Grab car straight to Hoi An (~30 km, 40–50 min) — 3 people plus bags don't fit a standard 4-seat comfortably. No Uber in Vietnam; Grab is the app.
AfternoonCheck in (2 rooms or a family room), nap, showers. Then a first slow walk into the Old Town.
EveningCooking class together — half-day classes (market tour + boat + the meal you cooked) typically run afternoon/evening sessions. Then the payoff: lantern-lit Old Town, lanterns on from about 17:30, a lantern boat on the Thu Bon River at dusk. The Old Town ticket covers 5 of the 22 heritage sites.

Day 10 · Mon Apr 26

★ Ba Na Hills & the Golden Bridge — the must-do

Night 2 of 6 in Hoi An. The Golden Hands are the day trip this whole route bends around.

The daily rule: early beats everything here — be standing on the bridge by 08:30–09:00. Between 10:00 and 15:00 it degrades into a 20-minute photo queue.
~07:00Leave Hoi An by private car for the day (one shared group cost) or a group tour. ~60 km, 1–1.5h.
08:30On the Golden Bridge at Sun World Ba Na Hills, 1,487 m up. Cable car up (5,801 m, one of the world's longest, 15–25 min) — the ticket includes the return cable car, the bridge, French Village, Fantasy Park, and the flower gardens.
MiddayFrench Village and the gardens at the top. Bring a layer each — the mountain runs 8–12°C cooler than Hoi An. Allow 4–6 hours on site.
AfternoonReturn leg to Hoi An by the same car/tour (its own route block below). Back for a late lunch or an easy afternoon, then one more lantern-lit evening in Hoi An.

Why this order works

The Loop sits at Days 4–6, after the jet lag fades and before trip fatigue sets in — it's the physical peak of the trip, and travelers rate it the highlight ("10/10… these 3 days were easily the highlight of my trip to Southeast Asia"). Ninh Binh and the train are the hinge, and Hoi An at the end is the recovery and the reward. Nothing in the core plan requires a domestic flight, and as a group of three you move as one private party through the Loop and the train cabin rather than mixing into larger tour groups.

Traveler accounts: Backpackers Wanderlust — Ha Giang Loop review · TripAdvisor — 3D2N Easy Rider reviews (snippets only)

Getting around — every leg, exactly, for 3

Each leg names the start and end point, method, distance, and time. For a party of three plus luggage, book the larger car (Grab 6/7-seat or private car) on every car leg. Fix this in your head before you land: there is no Uber in Vietnam — the app is Grab (Green SM and Be are local alternatives). Return legs are listed as their own legs. Every leg has its Google Maps route embedded under it.

Leg 1 — Airport into Hanoi

Noi Bai Airport (HAN) → Hanoi Old Quarter
Method: Larger Grab car for 3 + luggage (easiest) or Bus 86Distance: 27–30 kmTime: 35–60 min (75–90 at rush hour)

After 24+ hours of travel, take the larger Grab — order a 6/7-seat car in the app from the arrivals hall so the price is fixed before you ride and all three bags fit. No Uber in Vietnam. Bus 86 is the budget option (every 20–30 min, ~05:05–23:00, per-person fare) and ends at Hanoi Railway Station via the Old Quarter.

Open in Google Maps ↗

Sources: TravelGuidesTip · TourTeller

Leg 2 — Hanoi up to Ha Giang

Hanoi (Old Quarter pickup) → Ha Giang City
Method: Sleeper bus or limousine van — book 3 seats (usually booked by your Loop operator)Distance: ~300 kmTime: 7–8h sleeper bus · 6–7h limousine van

Day 4 morning departure in this plan, arriving Ha Giang City around midday to start Loop day 1. Operators named in the research: Hung Thanh, Bang Phan, Grouptour, Techbus VN, Kings Express. Most Loop packages include or arrange this transfer — confirm 3 seats and the exact pickup point when you book the Loop, and confirm where your big bags are stored (Hanoi or Ha Giang — Logistics).

Open in Google Maps ↗

Sources: VietnamTourism — 3 routes compared · Vexere Hanoi–Ha Giang

Leg 3 — The Loop itself

Ha Giang City → Yen Minh → Dong Van → Ma Pi Leng → Meo Vac → Ha Giang City
Method: Easy Rider — 3 passengers, each behind their own local driver (3 riders, 3 drivers)Time: 3 days, ~8am–5pm riding days

Not self-drive. The traveler consensus is near-unanimous: beginners do not drive this road themselves — unpaved sections, potholes, trucks, no guardrails. As passengers with experienced licensed drivers it's the highlight of the trip. Book a private or small-group tour for just the three of you where possible. Packages typically include the bike and fuel, guide, homestay private rooms (upgraded), all meals, helmet and rain gear, entrances, the Nho Que boat, and the border permit. See Logistics for where your luggage goes.

Open in Google Maps ↗

Sources: DayTripsVietnam — Loop cost guide · My Favourite Escapes — Loop safety, first-hand

Leg 4 — Ha Giang back to Hanoi (return leg)

Ha Giang City → Hanoi
Method: Sleeper bus — 3 berths (usually arranged by the Loop operator)Distance: ~300 kmTime: 7–8h

Day 6, after the final Loop leg: collect your stored luggage, shower at the hostel (operators typically include the stop), and board. If your big bags were stored at the operator's Hanoi office instead of Ha Giang, this is the bus that gets you back to them — you collect them in Hanoi before Leg 5.

Open in Google Maps ↗

Leg 5 — Hanoi down to Ninh Binh

Hanoi → Tam Coc, Ninh Binh
Method: Limousine van — 3 seats, hotel-to-hotelDistance: ~95 kmTime: 2–2.5h

Day 6 night, the second hop of the long travel day. The limousine van is the right call: it drops all three of you in Tam Coc itself, not at Ninh Binh city station 7–10 km away. If you rail it instead (soft seat), add a larger Grab from Ninh Binh station to Tam Coc — Grab, because there is no Uber in Vietnam.

Open in Google Maps ↗

Sources: Parfum d'Automne · Best of Ninh Binh

Leg 6 — Around Ninh Binh

Tam Coc → Trang An (and back) · Tam Coc → Ninh Binh Station
Method: Larger Grab car or guesthouse bicyclesTam Coc → Trang An: ~7 km · ~15 min each wayTam Coc → station: ~7–10 km · ~20 min

Two short hops, both Grab (no Uber in Vietnam). Day 7: Tam Coc → Trang An dock in the morning and the return leg Trang An → Tam Coc after the boat — order the Grab back from the dock. Day 8 evening: Tam Coc → Ninh Binh station for the 21:57 train, arriving well ahead of departure.

Open in Google Maps ↗ · Tam Coc → Station ↗

Leg 7 — The sleeper train south ★

Ninh Binh Station → Da Nang Station
Method: Overnight train SE19 (or SE3) — one whole 4-berth soft-sleeper cabin for the groupDistance: 676 kmSE19: dep 21:57 → arr 11:35 next daySE3: dep 21:36 → arr ~10:28–10:43 next dayBerths: buy all 4 berths so the cabin is exclusively yours

SE19 is the pick: a soft-sleeper-only train whose cabin is a lockable, air-conditioned 4-berth (2 lower + 2 upper) with bedding, reading lights, and charging outlets. For a party of 3 this is ideal: you fill 3 of the 4 berths — book all 4 so no stranger takes the fourth. Book lower berths where you can. Times differ by a few minutes between sources, so recheck on the official site when booking. Book only on dsvn.vn (the official railway; tickets open ~60 days ahead, names must match passports exactly for all 3) — look-alike sites are not official. If a foreign card fails on dsvn.vn, Baolau or 12Go Asia are the reliable fallbacks for a small fee.

Open in Google Maps ↗

Sources: Travelfish — Ninh Binh transport · Seat61 — Vietnam trains · Vexere — train fares

Leg 8 — Da Nang into Hoi An

Da Nang Station → Hoi An Old Town
Method: Larger Grab car for 3 + luggageDistance: ~30 kmTime: 40–50 min (60–90 at peak/rain)

Hoi An has no station or airport — Da Nang is its gateway in both directions. Off the train on Day 9, a larger Grab straight to your hotel is the zero-friction option for three plus bags. No Uber in Vietnam — Grab is the app.

Open in Google Maps ↗

Sources: Jungle Boss Tours · Da Nang Chill Ride

Leg 9 — Golden Bridge day trip, out ★ must-do

Hoi An → Sun World Ba Na Hills (Golden Bridge)
Where the hands are: Inside Sun World Ba Na Hills, 1,487 m up, ~25 km southwest of Da NangFrom Hoi An: ~60 km, 1–1.5h by carHours: 08:00–22:00

How to do it, for 3: leave Hoi An ~07:00 on Day 10 by private car (tickets extra — one shared cost for the group, not per person) or a group tour. The per-person ticket includes the return cable car — 5,801 m, one of the world's longest, 15–25 minutes — and the bridge, French Village, Fantasy Park, and flower gardens. Be standing on the bridge by 08:30–09:00; allow 4–6 hours on site and bring a layer each (the mountain runs 8–12°C cooler).

Open in Google Maps ↗

Sources: GoPlanReady — Sun World price list · Metta Voyage — Ba Na from Hoi An · Da Nang Transfer

Leg 10 — Golden Bridge day trip, return leg

Sun World Ba Na Hills → Hoi An Old Town
Method: Same private car / tour as the morningDistance: ~60 kmTime: 1–1.5hCost: Included in the day rate / tour price from Leg 9

Its own leg, not an afterthought: confirm the return pickup point at the cable-car base before you ride up in the morning, and agree the leave time then too. You're back in Hoi An by late afternoon on Day 10. Day 11 is a light Hoi An day, Days 12–14 are unplanned extra days, and Day 15 (May 1) is departure day.

Open in Google Maps ↗

Leg 11 — Home

Hoi An → Da Nang Airport (DAD) → Tampa / Orlando
Method: Larger Grab or private car for 3 + luggage, then your flightDistance: ~30 kmTime: 40–60 min drive

Same road as Leg 8 in reverse, on Day 15. Leave Hoi An ~4 hours before the 11:30 PM departure (VN430 DAD → ICN, then DL158 / DL1456 via Detroit, arriving Tampa 2:55 PM Sun May 2 — booked), together in one larger car — Grab, because there is no Uber in Vietnam. There is no direct bus worth planning around for a flight day.

Where you sleep — every night, for 3

Fourteen nights, and the page adds up: 1 on the plane, 2 in Hanoi, 2 on the Loop, 2 in Ninh Binh, 1 on the train, 6 in Hoi An (2 core nights Apr 25–26, the Day 11 night Apr 27, and 3 extra nights Apr 28–30). Hotel nights need 2 rooms or one triple / family room — a standard double won't fit three adults. No hotel is booked or named as "the" pick — each row gives the area to search and the room setup to look for. Hotels are not priced on this page, and neither is food — no price appears until there is a booking behind it.

Apr 17Night · Day 1
On the plane. Overnight long-haul — Kevin & Arwen booked (seats in Flights); land on Hanoi time.
Apr 18–192 nights · Days 2–3
Hanoi — a hotel in the Old Quarter with 2 rooms or a triple / family room. Status: Not booked. It's the walkable, food-dense base, where the airport car drops you and the Ha Giang transfer picks up. Ask about Day 4: bag storage after checkout if the Loop plan leaves your luggage with the hotel (see Logistics).
Apr 20–212 nights · Days 4–5
Loop homestays — included in the Easy Rider package; book the private-room upgrade for the group. Status: Not booked (part of the Loop booking). Default is a dorm bed in a village homestay; for three, pay the upgrade so the group gets private rooms (a double + a single/twin, or a family room where offered). Not booked separately — it's part of the Loop package.
Apr 22–232 nights · Days 6–7
Tam Coc, Ninh Binh — a guesthouse or small hotel in Tam Coc village with 2 rooms or a triple / family room. Status: Not booked. Not Ninh Binh city: Tam Coc puts you walking distance from the boat docks, Hang Mua, and dinner. Note the late arrival on Apr 22 when you book. Quieter alternative: around Trang An / Hoa Lu — prettier and calmer, but spread out, so you'd want bicycles for everything.
Apr 24Night · Day 8
On the SE19 sleeper train — one whole cabin for the group. Status: Not booked. A party of 3 fills 3 of the 4 berths in a lockable 4-berth soft-sleeper cabin — book all 4 berths so the cabin is exclusively yours and no fourth stranger shares (lower berths recommended).
Apr 25–306 nights · Days 9–14
Hoi An — a hotel in the Old Town / An Hoi area with 2 rooms or a family room. Status: Not booked. Core nights Apr 25–27 (Days 9–11) plus the extra nights Apr 28–30 for the unplanned Days 12–14; check out Sat May 1 for the 11:30 PM flight home. Lantern streets and restaurants on foot (busy evenings are the trade-off). Quieter option: An Bang Beach, 4–5 km away — beachfront places with the same 2-room / family-room need, 10–15 minutes into town by bike or Grab. Middle ground: Cam Thanh / rice-paddy homestays. April is Hoi An's sweet spot: dry season, roughly 24–30°C.
May 1Day 15
Travel day home from Da Nang. Check out of Hoi An on May 1 and fly from DAD at 11:30 PM on VN430 — night on the plane, via Seoul and Detroit, arriving Tampa 2:55 PM Sun May 2.

The one booking that sells out

Everything above is easy to find except the train cabin: sleepers sell out on weekends and holidays, and you need all 4 berths in the same cabin — April tickets only open ~60 days out on dsvn.vn. Set a reminder for mid-February 2027 and book SE19 the week it opens. Loop packages and Vietnam hotels (in the 2-room / triple setup above) can be booked much closer in.

Bags — where everything lives, leg by leg

Your luggage during the Loop — the open question, answered

None of your big bags go on the bikes. Every operator in the research stores them free — the choice to make when you book is where:

  • Option A — Hanoi: leave the main luggage at the Hanoi hotel (ask on Day 2) or the Loop operator's Hanoi office/storage (Jasmine and Ha Giang Vision both offer this). You travel to Ha Giang light and collect the bags on the way back through Hanoi on Day 6 — which this route does anyway.
  • Option B — Ha Giang: the operator's Ha Giang City hostel stores bags during the Loop — Jasmine stores excess luggage free at its Ha Giang hostel; QT includes storage; Bong has lockers at the hostel — bring your own padlocks (one per bag). You collect them on Day 6 before the bus south.
  • On the bike, each of you carries: a small daypack — 2–3 changes of light clothes, layers for cool mountain mornings, toiletries, charger, passport, cash. Rain gear is provided by operators.

Either option works; pick one and get it confirmed in writing with the operator booking, so Day 4 morning is not a negotiation.

Sources: PowerTraveller — Jasmine tour · TravelDudes — Loop guide · Ha Giang Vision

Movement & storage — every leg

  • Flights (Days 1 & 15): checked bags through to HAN out, home from DAD back (Kevin & Arwen). Carry-ons hold passports + a change of clothes.
  • HAN → hotel (Day 2): all bags in the larger Grab car with you.
  • Hanoi days (Days 2–3): bags in the hotel rooms.
  • Hanoi → Ha Giang (Day 4): daypacks only onward. Big bags go to the chosen storage (Hanoi hotel / operator Hanoi office, or operator's Ha Giang hostel if they ride the bus up with you — confirm at booking).
  • On the Loop (Days 4–6): daypack per rider, strapped to the bike. Nothing else moves.
  • Ha Giang → Hanoi → Ninh Binh (Day 6): collect bags from storage at whichever end holds them; count 3 big bags + 3 daypacks at the Ha Giang hostel, on the bus, and again at the Tam Coc check-in.
  • Ninh Binh (Days 7–8): bags at the guesthouse; pack a small cabin bag each for the train on Day 8.
  • Train (Day 8 night): everything travels with you — big bags in the cabin/luggage space of your own 4-berth cabin.
  • Da Nang → Hoi An → out (Days 9–15): all bags in the Grab cars with you; hotel storage after checkout on Day 15 if needed before the 11:30 PM flight.

Choosing a Loop operator — for a group of 3

Easy Rider package prices genuinely conflict between operator pages and resellers, so confirm the exact price and inclusions in writing before paying. Ask for a private or small-group departure for just your party (3 passengers + 3 drivers) and confirm the private-room homestay upgrade in writing:

  • Jasmine Tours — includes free hostel nights and storage in Hanoi + Ha Giang.
  • Bong Hostel — its own pages disagree on price — ask directly.
  • QT Motorbikes — 3-day Easy Rider without the Hanoi bus; packages with the sleeper bus run higher.

Since April 2026 the province requires motorbike tours to run through licensed operators with written contracts — another reason to book a named operator, not the cheapest offer.

Sources: PowerTraveller — Jasmine 3D2N · Bong Hostel — 2026 guide · Trail & Pass — QT

Loop safety — the honest version

The consensus from real riders: as Easy Rider passengers with a reputable operator, the Loop is the highlight of the trip — "I felt safe with my Easy Rider throughout… I'd rate the overall experience 10/10." It is not risk-free. In April 2026 a 19-year-old British passenger, Orla Wates, died after being thrown from a bike on the Loop and struck by a truck — the event that triggered the province's licensed-operator crackdown. The guardrails this plan follows for all three of you: passengers only, never self-drive as beginners (Vietnam only honors 1968-Convention IDPs for motorbikes; a US license alone doesn't qualify); book a licensed operator; speak up if your driver speeds; and each traveler checks their travel insurance covers riding as a motorbike passenger before you go. Expect sore knees and a numb seat by day three.

Sources: Backpackers Wanderlust — Loop review · My Favourite Escapes — "Is the Loop dangerous?" · The Guardian — Orla Wates, Apr 2026

Apps, money, and movement basics

  • Grab is the ride app — book the larger 6/7-seat car for the group; foreign cards work, English interface. There is no Uber in Vietnam. Green SM (electric) and Be are backups.
  • Cash matters on the Loop — it's the main payment method up there. Each of you carries dong for tips, drinks, and small stops; cards are fine in Hanoi / Hoi An hotels.
  • Buses and trains book through the operator, Vexere / 12Go Asia, or dsvn.vn for the train — 3 seats/berths together, and all 4 berths for the train cabin.
  • April weather: the north is in its dry season (Nov–Apr), but Ha Giang can still throw fog and rain, and Hanoi / Hoi An run hot and humid.

Sources: Travelness — Uber in Vietnam · Bento — ride-hailing in Vietnam

What to pack

  • Everyday: light, breathable clothes — Hanoi and Hoi An run hot and humid in April.
  • Layers: one warm layer each for Loop mornings and Ba Na Hills (8–12°C cooler at the top).
  • On the bike: the daypack kit from the luggage card — 2–3 changes, toiletries, charger, passport, cash — plus a small seat cushion each.
  • Footwear: broken-in walking shoes; sandals for Hoi An evenings.
  • Power: Vietnam uses Type A / C / F sockets, 220V — US plugs fit A sockets; bring one C adapter per person to be safe.
  • Phone & documents: power bank, padlock per big bag (Loop storage lockers), passports + booking confirmations saved offline.

They showed no seats on Korean Air's page because Delta manages them; likewise, Korean Air–operated legs show no seats on Delta's page because those seats live in Korean Air's system.

  • Day 6 timing: the Loop finish + Ha Giang → Hanoi → Ninh Binh chain is the trip's longest day (~9–11 hours of road after the final ride). If the operator offers a through-arrangement, take it; if the chain can't be made in one evening, the fallback is a Hanoi night and Ninh Binh the next morning — which costs a Ninh Binh night.
  • Train times wobble by minutes between Travelfish, Seat61, and Vexere (SE3 arrival 10:28 vs 10:43). Recheck on dsvn.vn at booking.
  • Loop prices conflict by channel — the same operator shows different prices on different pages, and Bong's own pages disagree. Confirm inclusions and the private/small-group + private-room setup in writing.
  • Hoi An → Ba Na Hills distance is 60–62 km in most sources, 42–45 km in one — the 1–1.5h drive time is the number to plan around.
  • Hotels and food are not priced on this page — no price is shown until there is a booking or receipt behind it.

Alternate plan — Ha Long Bay added, for 3

Ha Long Bay is an alternate only — it is not in the core 15-day route. On this 15-day trip it fits only by spending two nights: one Ninh Binh night and one Hoi An night. Here is exactly what that swap looks like, so the trade is a decision, not an accident.

Where it would slot

Between Hanoi and Ninh Binh, using the Day 6–7 window: instead of riding the Loop's return straight through to Ninh Binh on Day 6 and spending two nights there, the cruise takes one of those Ninh Binh nights, and Hoi An gives up its second night to keep the May 1 flight home. The sleeper train and the Ba Na Hills must-do do not move.

What changes, day by day

  • Days 1–5: unchanged — flights, Hanoi buffer, Loop days 1–2 for 3.
  • Day 6 (Apr 22): Loop day 3, bus back to Hanoi as in the core plan — then the night is spent in Hanoi or on the early cruise transfer rather than continuing to Ninh Binh. Ninh Binh loses this night.
  • Day 7 (Apr 23): cruise limousine from the Old Quarter (~08:00–08:45) to Ha Long, board at midday: 2 cabins for the group (cruise cabins are built for 2 — a party of 3 needs a double + a single/twin, or a rare triple), lunch, kayaking, Sung Sot cave. Night on the boat.
  • Day 8 (Apr 24): Tai chi at dawn, brunch, back in Hanoi ~15:00, limousine van to Tam Coc by evening, SE19 sleeper train that night (whole cabin, as in the core plan) — Ninh Binh becomes a pass-through instead of a 2-night stay, and Trang An / Hang Mua come off the plan.
  • Day 9 (Apr 25): Hoi An as in the core plan — Old Town and cooking class.
  • Day 10 (Apr 26): Ba Na Hills stays — it's the must-do. Hoi An's slack is the other night the bay costs: the slow second-day breathing room disappears, and any delay anywhere now lands directly on the Ba Na Hills day or the flight home.
  • Day 11 (Apr 27): light Hoi An morning, as in the core plan — no flight today.
  • Days 12–15 (Apr 28 – May 1): the core plan's unplanned extra days stay unplanned in this alternate too, and the flight home is Day 15 (May 1) from DAD.

What it takes — for 3

A 2-day / 1-night cruise (named examples in the research: Calypso, Luxury Rosy, and 5-star options) assumes 2 cabins for the group — confirm the 3-person cabin arrangement when booking, as a single supplement may apply to the single-occupancy cabin. Included per person: balcony cabin, all meals on board, kayaking, cave visit, Ti Top Island, tai chi, cooking demo, guide, entrance fees, and the round-trip Hanoi limousine. Not included: drinks, tips, spa.

The real price is the two nights: one from Ninh Binh (Trang An and Hang Mua go), one from Hoi An (the slow second day goes). What you get for them is the postcard — and what travelers in the consensus research flagged as the most packaged, tour-group-feeling stop on the whole route. The quieter alternative the research points to: sail Lan Ha Bay instead (same karsts, fewer boats, better swimming).

Sources: CityBreakGeek — cruise guide · The Abroad Guide — Calypso · PowerTraveller — all-inclusive cruise

Bottom line: on the 15-day plan the bay is expensive in nights, not in days — it costs one Ninh Binh night and one Hoi An night, and the core route's Trang An boat ride already gives you the same karst landscape from a small boat, without the cruise crowds. It stays on this tab unless the three of you vote it in.

The final plan — 15 days, Sat Apr 17 – Sat May 1, 2027, for Kevin, Arwen, and Evan. Built from two research passes checked November 2026: a traveler-consensus report (Reddit, TripAdvisor, Bogleheads, and first-hand blogs — Reddit/TripAdvisor quotes are search snippets, since both sites blocked full reads) and a logistics report (KAYAK, momondo, Travelfish, Seat61, Vexere, Sun World pricing, and operator pages).
